To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the molar Ti:TiC ratio must be adjusted in a way that nonstoichiometric (Ti,Mo,V,Cr)C0.5 is formed.
TiB and TiCy particles can be synthesized successfully by solid-state reaction of Ti-5553 with B4C particles and graphite, respectively.
TiB/TiCy particle-reinforced Ti-5553 matrix composites were successfully synthesized by solid-state reactions with B4C particles and carbon during SPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the solid-state reaction kinetics of B4C with titanium and the formation of TiB/TiCy particles in the TMCs.
the solid-state reaction kinetics of the TMC formation, the microstructure of the TMC, and its effect on the mechanical properties.
the influence of the matrix alloying on the solid-state reaction kinetics, which is a key factor for the synthesis of TMCs by SPS with the solid-state reaction mechanism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the synthesis of in-situ TiB and TiCy particle-reinforced TMCs, a stoichiometric molar TiB0.5:TiC0.5 ratio is recommended.
the formation of stoichoimetric TiC is not possible during SPS and nonstoichiometric particles are formed instead.
the solid-state reaction kinetics are slowed down due to the formation of solid solutions of the matrix alloying constituents within the reinforcing particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TMCs with TiB:TiCy ratios of 1:0.5, which were synthesized by SPS, exhibit a hardness of 800 HV, a compressive strength of 1,600 MPa and bending strengths of up to 1,200 MPa.
the solid-state reaction kinetics can be improved by the use of matrix alloys containing alloying elements with a low solid solubility for carbon.
the molar Ti:TiC ratio should be kept as high as possible to achieve the highest possible hardness of the TMC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties of TMCs can be improved significantly with respect to the matrix alloy and the molar TiC:TiB ratio.
the solid-state reaction kinetics can be controlled by adjusting the molar Ti: B: C ratio and the matrix composition.

the mechanical properties of in-situ TiB and TiCy particle-reinforced TMCs can be adjusted successfully by adjusting the TiB:TiCy ratio and that the matrix alloying influences the solid-state reaction kinetics.
